toelichting: FICTIONAL: seven invented Helix Labs meeting transcripts for Phase 1a. Every name, figure and company is made up. 'expected' = the decisions the system should end up with after the rule checks (decision is matched by meaning; flags are checked by decision_contains). 'all_hands_must_exclude' = terms that must never appear in the all-hands text. Labels the transcript does not state are expected as leadership_only with the flag label_needs_review.

cases.name: 1 Normal: onboarding and pricing
cases.note: Two clean decisions with owner and date.
cases.input:
[FICTIONAL: Helix Labs is an invented company; all people and figures are made up.]
Mara: Thanks all. Three topics today: onboarding, pricing page, hiring.
Jon: Onboarding first. Trial users drop off at the data-import step.
Mara: What do we do about it?
Jon: I propose a guided import wizard. It delays the reporting feature by about two weeks.
Priya: I can live with that delay. Activation is our Q2 goal, so this is the priority.
Mara: Agreed. Jon owns the wizard, ready by 28 April.
Jon: Fine. I'll share the plan in the all-hands as well.
Mara: Good. Next, the pricing page.
Priya: Customers are confused by three plans. I'd cut it to two: Team and Business.
Lena: Sales is fine with that, as long as we keep the annual discount.
Mara: Decision: two plans from 1 May, Priya owns the page. Annual discount stays.
Priya: The trade-off is that we lose the cheap Starter plan and some small customers.
Mara: Accepted. That one can go in the all-hands too.
Jon: Hiring?
Mara: Nothing to decide today, we look again next week.
Mara: Thanks everyone.

decisions.label: all_hands
decisions.trade_off: reporting feature delayed about two weeks

decisions.decision: move from three plans to two (Team and Business)
decisions.label: all_hands
decisions.trade_off: lose Starter plan and some small customers

expected.comment: Hiring is open with no decision; it must not appear as a decision.

cases.name: 2 Normal: support and roadmap
cases.input:
[FICTIONAL: Helix Labs is an invented company; all people and figures are made up.]
Mara: Let's start with support load.
Lena: Tickets are up 30 percent since the launch.
Jon: Most are about export. A fix is two days of work.
Mara: Then do it. Jon owns the export fix, done by Friday 14 March.
Lena: And I'd like a status page so customers stop writing in.
Mara: Yes. Lena owns the status page, live by 21 March.
Priya: Goal is to bring tickets under 400 a month, that is the support OKR.
Mara: Good. Now the roadmap.
Priya: Option one, mobile app. Option two, API v2. I'd say API v2 first, it unlocks two partners.
Jon: The mobile app waits until Q4 then.
Mara: Decision for leadership only, we don't announce it yet: API v2 first, owner Priya, start in April.
Priya: The cost is that the mobile app slips to Q4.
Mara: Yes. Keep it inside this group until partners are told.
Lena: Understood.
Mara: That's it for today.

decisions.label: leadership_only
decisions.goal_or_okr: support OKR: under 400 tickets a month

decisions.label: leadership_only
decisions.goal_or_okr: support OKR: under 400 tickets a month

decisions.decision: build API v2 before the mobile app
decisions.label: leadership_only

cases.name: 3 Decision without owner
cases.input:
[FICTIONAL: Helix Labs is an invented company; all people and figures are made up.]
Mara: Security questionnaire from the Orbit account came in again.
Lena: They want proof of an external security review before signing.
Jon: We should do one. It costs about the same as one month of cloud spend.
Priya: Agreed, we need it for enterprise deals anyway.
Mara: So we decide: we get an external security review before the end of Q3.
Lena: Who runs it?
Mara: Let's see. Someone should pick it up.
Jon: I'm busy with the release.
Priya: Me too, until June.
Mara: OK, we leave the owner for now.
Lena: Next topic: office move.
Mara: Lease ends in August. Decision: we stay in the current office another year, Lena handles it with the landlord by 30 June.
Lena: Fine.
Mara: Share the office news in the all-hands.
Jon: Anything else?
Mara: No. Thanks.

decisions.decision: stay in the current office another year
decisions.label: all_hands

cases.name: 4 Decision reversed later
cases.note: Webinar series is agreed, then cancelled.
cases.input:
[FICTIONAL: Helix Labs is an invented company; all people and figures are made up.]
Mara: Marketing plan for the autumn.
Priya: I'd like a monthly webinar series starting in September.
Lena: Sales likes it. Leads from webinars convert well.
Mara: Decision: monthly webinar series, Priya owns it, first one 10 September.
Jon: Who hosts them? Engineering has no time.
Priya: Then I'd need a freelancer.
Mara: Hmm. Budget for the freelancer is not there.
Lena: Without it Priya runs everything alone.
Priya: That is not realistic next to the website work.
Mara: You're right. Reversing that: no webinar series this autumn.
Mara: Instead we write one case study per month. Priya owns it, first one by 15 September.
Lena: Good, I can bring two customers.
Priya: The trade-off is less live contact with prospects.
Mara: Accepted.
Jon: Fine by me.
Mara: Share the case-study plan with everyone, please.
Priya: Will do.

decisions.decision: write one customer case study per month
decisions.label: all_hands

expected.comment: The reversed 'monthly webinar series' (10 September) must be dropped. The final 'no webinar series' item is kept, without owner or date, and stays out of the all-hands text.

cases.name: 5 Same decision mentioned twice
cases.note: The support-hours decision comes up at the start and again at the end.
cases.input:
[FICTIONAL: Helix Labs is an invented company; all people and figures are made up.]
Mara: First item: support hours.
Lena: Customers in the US write at night. I propose extended support until 20:00.
Jon: That means a late shift. Who covers it?
Lena: Two of my team volunteered, I own the rollout.
Mara: Decision: extend support hours until 20:00 starting 5 May, Lena owns it.
Priya: Does that touch the OKR?
Lena: Yes, first response time under four hours is the Q2 support goal.
Mara: Good. Second item: the blog redesign.
Priya: I'd postpone it until after summer so we can finish the docs.
Mara: Decision: postpone the blog redesign to September, Priya owns it.
Jon: Fine.
Priya: Any other business?
Lena: Just to confirm, support runs until 20:00 from the fifth of May, right?
Mara: Yes, extended support until eight in the evening from 5 May, Lena.
Jon: Great, then we're done.
Mara: Thanks everyone.

decisions.label: leadership_only
decisions.goal_or_okr: Q2 support goal: first response under four hours

expected.comment: Passes with one merged support-hours item, whether the model or the rule merged it.

cases.name: 6 Board item next to a product decision
cases.note: Fundraising talk must not reach the all-hands text.
cases.input:
[FICTIONAL: Helix Labs is an invented company; all people and figures are made up.]
Mara: Two things: the Series A and the dashboard launch.
Mara: Board only for now: we start Series A talks in June with two lead investors. Target raise is 12 million.
Lena: Who talks to the investors?
Mara: I do. Nothing of this goes outside this room, not even to the team.
Jon: Understood. And the valuation range?
Mara: Also board only. We don't discuss it beyond this call.
Priya: OK. Now the dashboard.
Priya: The new dashboard is ready for beta. I'd open it to all customers on 2 June.
Jon: Support needs a week to prepare.
Priya: Then 9 June.
Mara: Decision: the new dashboard launches to all customers on 9 June. Priya owns the launch.
Priya: It supports the Q2 goal of weekly active users.
Jon: The trade-off is that we freeze other front-end work for a month.
Mara: Yes, accepted. Tell the whole company about the dashboard.
Lena: I'll draft the customer email.
Mara: Fine. Series A stays quiet.
Priya: Agreed.
Mara: Thanks.

decisions.decision: start Series A talks with two lead investors
decisions.label: board_only

decisions.decision: launch the new dashboard to all customers
decisions.label: all_hands
decisions.trade_off: other front-end work frozen for a month

cases.name: 7 Misheard model or partner name
cases.note: Names are written wrong in the transcript; flag low confidence, do not correct.
cases.input:
[FICTIONAL: Helix Labs is an invented company; all people and figures are made up.]
Mara: Next topic: the model for the summary feature.
Jon: I tested Claude Sonet and it was good enough. The cost is about half of what we pay now.
Priya: And the other option was Gemmini Flash?
Jon: Yes, but quality was lower on long documents.
Mara: Decision: we move the summary feature to Claude Sonet. Jon owns the switch, done by 20 June.
Jon: The trade-off is that we depend on one vendor for summaries.
Mara: Accepted.
Lena: Partner news: we sign with Dataflo, or Dataflow, I can't read my notes.
Mara: Dataflo, I think. Decision: Lena owns the partner announcement draft, due 15 June.
Lena: I'll check the right spelling with them first.
Priya: Please do, before anything goes out.
Jon: For the summary model, I'll run a last quality check before the switch.
Mara: Good. Share the summary model change with the team after the switch.
Jon: Will do.
Lena: The partner draft stays inside leadership until it is signed.
Mara: Thanks all.

decisions.decision: move the summary feature to Claude Sonet
decisions.label: all_hands
decisions.trade_off: depend on one vendor for summaries

decisions.decision: draft the partner announcement for Dataflo
decisions.label: leadership_only
